narthēcĭum , ii, n., = ναρθήκιον (lit. a piece of narthex-wood which has been hollowed out for keeping ointments and medicines in;
I. “hence any vessel in which these articles are kept),” an ointment-box, a medicine-chest, Mart. 14, 78, 1 : “jam doloris medicamenta illa Epicurea tamquam de narthecio proment,” Cic. Fin. 2, 7, 22 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
